title: An Ore-type Theorem for Oriented Discrepancy of Hamilton Cycles
summary: Oriented discrepancy concerns the existence of prescribed subgraphs whose edges exhibit a substantial imbalance between the two directions. The Hamilton cycle case was first investigated by Gishboliner, Krivelevich, and Michaeli. Subsequently, Freschi and Lo established a sharp minimum-degree result and raised the question of whether a corresponding Ore-type theorem holds. For an oriented graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, define $σ_2(G):=\min\{d_G(x)+d_G(y):x\neq y,\ xy,yx\notin E(G)\},$ with $σ_2(G):=2(n-1)$ when $G$ is a tournament.
